text:
Recent work supports learning temporal relevance while retaining older history. [TemProxRec (2024)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.09784) combines absolute and relative temporal/positional embeddings in self-attention, plus contrastive learning across interactions occurring in similar periods. It directly motivates distinguishing equal positional distances with different elapsed times. [Parameter-Efficiently Leveraging Session Information (2025)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/abstract/document/10902109) investigates session tokens, session segment embeddings and temporal self-attention with little additional parameter overhead. [ScaleRec (2026 issue)](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0306457325002596) models transient interests and persistent preferences through multiple sequence scales, local Gaussian attention and adaptive long-term preference aggregation. These papers motivate temporal modeling; they do not establish gains under the pinned RecHarness evaluation.

A compatible experimental hypothesis is one BERT4Rec network with jointly learned per-head relative-position and bucketed elapsed-time attention biases, allowing different heads to emphasize recent intent or durable preferences without deleting older interactions. This is an inference from the literature, not a verified result. Preserve [BERT4Rec’s masked-item objective](https://arxiv.org/abs/1904.06690) and appended-mask inference. Compute temporal features exclusively from observed history; give the appended mask a learned unknown-time treatment rather than using the held-out target timestamp. Compare position-only, time-only and combined biases under identical seeds, training limits and macro validation HR@10, with one checkpoint per category.
